quizzes.title: Chagos Sovereignty Deal and the Diego Garcia Base
quizzes.passage: Britain has agreed to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. The UK and Mauritius reached this agreement, and the UK ceded its claims over the archipelago. The arrangement is not a complete handover, because the UK keeps sovereign rights over Diego Garcia, where a joint UK-US military base is located. Under the agreement, the base will remain operational for an initial period. The Chagos Islands are an archipelago in the Indian Ocean. The United States has raised concerns about the arrangement. Washington sees a change in sovereignty as a matter that could affect its strategic position, and that concern is part of a wider debate. The issue pits decolonisation against security interests. It also reflects a tension between international legal norms and realpolitik. Geopolitics adds another layer. Competition in the Indian Ocean region involves China, the United States and other regional powers. The UK has insisted that the issue should remain a bilateral matter. In 2015, Mauritius began legal proceedings against the UK at the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, challenging the UK's sovereignty claims and the forced removal of Chagossians. Mauritius is an island nation located in the Western Indian Ocean, and India has backed Mauritius's territorial claim over the archipelago.

questions.explanation: The agreement keeps the joint base operational for an initial period of 99 years.

questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Chagos archipelago comprises 58 islands.

quizzes.title: Colonial Passage of the Chagos Islands
quizzes.passage: The Chagos Islands are an archipelago in the Indian Ocean, and their history has been shaped by the European powers that controlled them. The islands were first reached by European sailors, and for a period they were under the control of a European power other than Britain. The turning point came when Britain took control of both the Chagos Islands and Mauritius, following a major conflict in Europe. Under the arrangements that followed, the islands passed into British hands. Britain later declared the Chagos Islands a British Indian Ocean Territory. Mauritius later argued that it had been coerced into giving up the islands during its colonial period. It pointed to a UN resolution that prohibited the breakup of colonies before independence. The UK, in turn, argued that the matter lay outside the reach of the body that had been asked to decide it. Mauritius later gained independence from British rule, and the dispute over the islands has a long history. Since then, the dispute has been pursued through legal action by Mauritius, and India has backed Mauritius's territorial claim over the Chagos Islands. Mauritius is an island nation located in the Western Indian Ocean. Today the dispute is between the UK and Mauritius.

quizzes.title: MAHASAGAR and Maritime Initiatives
quizzes.passage: MAHASAGAR is an initiative launched by the Indian Navy. It is an expanded framework that builds upon India's earlier maritime doctrine. While that doctrine primarily addressed India's immediate maritime neighbourhood, MAHASAGAR widens its scope to a broader group of countries. The key focus areas of the initiative are trade for development, mutual security, technology sharing and financial assistance. The initiative convenes naval chiefs and maritime officials from littoral states, including Bangladesh, Comoros, Kenya, Madagascar and Maldives. One of the new tools under the initiative is a platform called IOS Sagar, which is meant to deepen naval cooperation with Indian Ocean littorals. The platform focuses on humanitarian assistance, disaster relief and joint security efforts. Another new initiative is AIKEYME, a large-scale naval exercise. India served as the first responder for Mauritius during COVID-19. Mauritius participates in India-led VARUNA and MILAN naval drills. Mauritius conferred its highest civilian honour, the Grand Commander of the Order of the Star and Key of the Indian Ocean, on Prime Minister Modi. Mauritius serves as a key gateway for Indian trade and investment. Mauritius is a former British and French colony. Mauritius is a member of the Colombo Security Conclave with Sri Lanka, Maldives and Bangladesh.
